We consider all applicants for employment and provide reasonable accommodations for individuals with disabilities—please let us know through this form. Before you apply If you’ve applied before but didn't receive an offer, we recommend waiting at least one year before applying again. Bending Spoons is a demanding environment. We’re extremely ambitious and we hold ourselves—and one another—to a high standard. At Spot Solutions, we've incorporated Agentic AI deeply into our development process. Used properly, we've found that it can make an experienced developer dramatically more productive — in some projects, allowing us to deliver software roughly twice as fast as we could previously. We're looking for an experienced developer who wants to work this way. This is not an "AI job” It's a software development job where AI is becoming one of your most powerful tools. You'll still need to understand architecture, databases, APIs, security, testing, maintainability and what makes software actually useful to the people who have to use it. The difference is that you'll have AI agents helping you write, understand, test and improve that software. We use tools such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Visual Studio and VS Code , and we're continually experimenting with better ways to use multiple models and agents. If you've already gone well beyond basic AI-assisted coding, we'd love to talk to you. If you haven't, but you're an excellent developer who is curious about this new way of working, we'd also like to talk to you. The unusual part of this job We're looking for someone who can move between custom software development and Microsoft 365/SharePoint development. That isn't accidental. One day you might be building a C#/.NET web application and integrating it with a business system.   The next day you might be: Designing a SharePoint solution Building a Power Automate workflow Creating a Power App   Migrating content with ShareGate Writing PowerShell   Working with Microsoft Graph Figuring out how to move a client's existing business process into Microsoft 365 We don't automatically write custom software when a Power Platform solution is better. And we don't force a low-code solution onto a problem that really needs custom software. We choose the technology that best solves the problem. That's one of the things that makes this role interesting. What you'll bring We're looking for a strong developer with: Strong experience C# / .NET Web applications and APIs SQL / relational databases Git Visual Studio and/or VS Code Software architecture and application design Meaningful Microsoft 365 experience SharePoint Online Power Apps and/or Power Automate PowerShell Microsoft Graph ShareGate or another migration platform Useful additional experience Azure Dataverse Power BI SPFx JavaScript HTML / CSS / JSON Other programming languages such as Python, PHP or Java AI experience We're particularly interested in people who have used AI agents for more than autocomplete or generating a few functions. Someone who: Gets genuinely interested when faced with a problem they've never solved before Can look at a business process and figure out what technology should — and shouldn't — be involved Doesn't confuse a technically impressive solution with a useful solution Can explain technical concepts to a business user Cares about the quality of the software they leave behind Is comfortable admitting "I don't know" and then figuring it out Enjoys learning Isn't afraid of new technology — but isn't impressed by technology simply because it's new What you'll get You'll work on different problems, with different clients, using different technologies. You'll work alongside experienced developers and consultants who have spent years building everything from custom business applications to SharePoint and Microsoft 365 solutions. You'll also get a front-row seat to something we think is going to fundamentally change software development: using Agentic AI as part of the development process rather than simply as a coding assistant. And, because we're in Vancouver: Gastown location Close to SkyTrain Rooftop deck Friday lunches and knowledge-sharing Team events Snacks and drinks Flexible work environment Super Flexible Time Banking Competitive compensation and benefits Interested? What's the most interesting software you've built, and what did it accomplish? 2. What have you personally done with SharePoint/Microsoft 365? 3. What's the most sophisticated way you've used AI in software development? Those answers will tell us much more than a list of buzzwords. Come build useful things with us.

review_candidates.title: Staff Developer - Cloud Engineering
review_candidates.description: About The Role Hi, I'm Scott, and I lead the Cloud Engineering team at Jane. I've spent a couple of decades keeping large platforms running and scaling at companies like Loblaw and Achievers, and I joined Jane to help our platform meet its next stage of growth. Cloud Engineering owns the infrastructure that underpins the whole Jane platform. We keep it running, monitor it, scale it, and add capacity as our clinics grow. We're also the team people come to when they aren't sure where a problem belongs, so we end up working across almost every part of engineering. Our platform has served Jane well for more than a decade, and we're now approaching an inflection point. A big part of this role is figuring out what it takes to scale it cleanly for the company's next stage of growth. You'll work alongside other Staff engineers in our team to help shape the long-term vision for our infrastructure alongside our staff and senior staff engineers, then break that vision into pieces we can start delivering now. Just as important as the technical work is how you show up. The team needs a driver: someone who runs at hard, ambiguous problems, is often first to jump in and help, and can bring several teams together to build consensus to land big ideas. We can't scale Jane on our own, so building partnerships and championing change is core to the job. You'll work with a modern, cloud-native stack at real scale, with plenty of room to raise the bar for how we use our tools, including AI. If you like solving gnarly infrastructure problems and making everyone around you more effective, I'd love to meet you. What Impact We're Looking For You To Make Help set the longer-term technical vision for Jane's infrastructure alongside our staff and senior staff engineers, then turn that vision into concrete pieces the team can deliver along the way. Act as a driver on hard, ambiguous problems, looking past the symptom to the real issue and seeing it through to resolution even when it spans several teams. Champion change across engineering by building the relationships and consensus needed to land big infrastructure improvements, since scaling Jane is never a solo effort. Provide technical leadership to other teams, helping them design cloud infrastructure for new features and make sound architectural choices. Improve day-to-day operational health by reducing noisy alerts, hardening the platform, and making the whole system easier to run. Work closely with our Application Security Team to harden our infrastructure against security and compliance requirements. Bring an AI-positive mindset, helping the team get more leverage from AI tooling while respecting that infrastructure changes carry a real blast radius. What Experience We Need Deep expertise with AWS, including multi-region deployments and high-scale, highly available cloud services. Strong command of infrastructure as code, particularly Terraform. Solid infrastructure architecture skills, with a clear sense of how to assemble AWS building blocks into scalable, reliable systems. Experience operating databases at scale. Including upgrades, scaling, performance tuning and capacity planning. A track record of running large projects and driving consensus across many stakeholders. For this role, that attitude and problem-solving ability matter to us as much as raw technical depth. Can you look past a symptom to find the real problem, then work across several teams to get it solved? Experience operating at a company of meaningful scale that's growing quickly, ideally with a "been there, done that" perspective on scaling infrastructure through rapid growth. You're comfortable somewhere between a small startup and a large enterprise, in that fast-growth middle. An AI-positive mindset and hands-on experience using AI as a coding and research tool, with the judgment to know when to direct it and when to step in. At the staff level, we expect you to guide these tools well and explain the decisions behind your work. Comfort participating in an on-call rotation. Staff engineers here act as technical leaders, so we're looking for someone who sets direction, raises the bar, and lifts up the people around them.. If you don't meet every single qualification but are excited about this role, we'd still love to hear from you. More About Jane Jane is a founder-led, high-growth SaaS company with a remote-first team working across Canada, the US, and the UK, united by our mission to help the helpers. This role is remote first. We are not hybrid. We build the products and tools that thousands of clinics rely on every day to run their businesses, care for their patients, and grow their communities. That level of impact means every person at Jane plays an important role in how we show up for our customers. We're all responsible for being deeply connected to their needs, obsessed with improving their experience, and proud of the difference our work makes in their day-to-day lives. Jane is growing fast, and that growth brings exciting challenges that call for adaptability, resilience, learning agility, and humility. We're proud of what we've built and quick to admit what we don't know yet. We listen, learn, and adjust as we go. More than 70,000 businesses run on Jane which has 250,000+ practitioners interacting with our product on a daily basis and growth is continuing to accelerate. Our goal isn't just delivery - it's delight. We move quickly, communicate openly, and solve real problems together. If you're energized by ambiguity, motivated by impact, and eager to learn with others, you'll thrive at Jane. Compensation & Benefits At Jane, we’re committed to paying fairly, clearly, and above all, paying for growth. This role has an annual salary range of $158,400 to $247,500. While that is a large range, it is intentional. It reflects the full growth journey someone might take in the role, from developing skills early on to becoming highly proficient and ultimately achieving excellence. Most new hires join at the accomplished stage, which for this role represents an annual salary of $188,100 . A starting salary below this typically indicates a candidate with strong potential who is still developing key skills. Salaries above this usually apply to existing team members who have made a significant impact and bring deep Jane-specific knowledge. We believe in paying for growth . You’ll have regular career development conversations with your manager and your compensation will grow as you gain experience and contribute meaningfully to our mission. Paying clearly is one of our compensation fundamentals. Watch this short video to learn how our salary bands are set. You’re also encouraged to ask questions about compensation at any point during the interview process. We also offer a comprehensive benefits package, You can learn more about it here ! Jane takes job scams and candidate fraud seriously. Jane will only contact you from an @ jane.app email address. We'll never contact you from a personal email, ask for payment, or request purchases during the hiring process. If something doesn't seem right, please reach out to us at hiring@jane.app before sharing any personal information.

review_candidates.title: Platform Engineer
review_candidates.description: About Us Ticket Tailor is committed to empowering a diverse range of event creators through simple and affordable ticketing. But that's not all, we're also on a mission to make sure that every single ticket sold has a positive impact on all stakeholders, our team, our planet and the communities we operate in. We call this "Growth on Purpose" and are proud to be a Certified B Corp™, officially putting business for good at the centre of everything we do. Last year, over 10 million orders were placed through the Ticket Tailor platform, for all types of events from art installations to water parks. We have a world-class NPS score, and pride ourselves in building a simple platform built with a customer-first mindset. We're a fully independent, profitable, and bootstrapped company meaning we don't have to answer to anyone except ourselves and our customers, allowing us to scale the company sustainably and with soul. We work hybrid-remote and do two days per week in office, in our lovely space in Hackney. About The Role We're growing our Platform team, and hiring a full-time Platform Engineer to be our third member. It's a real mix of work: one day you will be building a system to protect our servers from high traffic influxes, reworking a Terraform module the next, then adopting a new self-hosted tool that unlocks teams. You'll own the infrastructure everything else runs on, taking real ownership of how it comes together. The impact you have on the people around you is what will motivate you, and the problem will interest you as much as the tools you solve it with. You'll work alongside two other Platform Engineers and close to the product engineers, pairing, reviewing, unblocking, and shaping the platform together. Like the rest of engineering, we lean on tools like Claude to move faster because it changes what three people can realistically own. Everything you deliver is yours end to end, from spotting the problem worth solving to running it in production. As part of a small team you'll have a real say in the technology decisions and share in the successes with the whole company. What You'll Do Design, build and maintain our infrastructure, from MySQL and Aurora through to ECS and Cloudflare, managed as code in Terraform. Bring ideas for tooling and improvements that would have real impact, then take ownership of building them once we agree they're worth it. Support reliability and observability, using Datadog to make sure we find out about problems before our customers do. Take part in the operational work: migrations, upgrades, incident response and troubleshooting production issues, staying calm and methodical when it matters. Use AI tools creatively and fluently to amplify your impact, reaching for new tools and ways of working rather than defaulting to how things have always been done. Bring judgement on infrastructure design that others can lean on, keeping things simple rather than reaching for complexity we'd have to live with. What we're looking for Essential A deep understanding of AWS, evidenced by owning production infrastructure across multiple services (EC2 | ECS | RDS | Lambda | VPC | SQS). Infrastructure as code as your default, with experience maintaining a Terraform estate. Real depth with relational databases: schema migrations, failovers, upgrades and performance work. Experience with containerisation in production. A genuine drive to work in an AI-native way - you're curious and happy to change how you work as the tools evolve. This is core to how our team operates. Experience using AI and agentic tools to amplify your impact, with a view on the risks when agents reach production. Strong system design skills - you can tell when a problem needs solving properly versus quickly. Desirable Awareness of PCI DSS and what building to that standard demands is a plus. Experience with Cloudflare or a similar edge platform (DNS | WAF | Cache | Workers). Experience building PHP applications is desirable but not essential. PHP is our primary stack, with tooling in Python and Node, so familiarity with either of those is useful. Strong engineers from any modern language will be considered. How you work Keep it simple. You don't overcomplicate, you reason from first principles, and you know when to be pragmatic and when to polish. You’re ambitious to take long-term ownership of the payments product, building a sustainable, extendable, maintainable codebase. Focused on impact. You have a deep care and empty for event organisers and you're excited to watch adoption and revenue grow, using signals to iterate and improve. You’re security minded and you build with care and awareness so things can’t be exploited. Driven by feedback. You have a growth mindset and see feedback as a tool for getting better. Human after all. You're happiest when working as part of a team. You thrive in working in kind, collaborative spaces where you can be vulnerable and transparent. At Ticket Tailor, we’re passionate about creating a diverse and inclusive environment where people can thrive, be inspired, and feel comfortable to be themselves. As a Certified B Corp™, we lead from the front, and with purpose, to disrupt the ticketing industry while ensuring we accommodate and celebrate people of all backgrounds along the way. We believe that diverse teams enable us to have different perspectives and points of view, making us even stronger in achieving our goals. We encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply and join us on our mission. Level of role We’re open to hiring at either mid or senior level, depending on your experience and the scope of responsibility you’ve held. The upper end of our salary range (£75,000+) is intended for candidates joining us at Senior level. At either level, you’ll have a real say in the technical and product decisions we make. For a Senior level position we would expect strong experience and evidence in shaping solutions and contributing to key development decisions, such as choosing a direction while the requirements were still moving, bringing engineers and the business with you, and staying close enough to the solution to understand whether those decisions worked in practice. Our Tools 🦿PHP is our primary language, and we use Laminas and Mezzio frameworks 🤖 AI is woven into how we work, using Claude Code and agentic development workflows 🫘 OpenTofu / Terraform for infrastructure definitions 👮 Open Policy Agent for policy as code 📐 Linear for project management, Notion for docs 🌐 AWS for servers, databases and storage 🌥️ Cloudflare for CDN, queueing and workers 🌊 Github and Github Actions for source control and CI 🧑‍🚒 Incident.io for incident management 🐕 Datadog for logging, monitoring and metrics The Process If your application is shortlisted, then you will receive detailed information about the next stages of the process. As an outline, the process will include: An initial discovery call to learn more about you, your motivation, suitability for the position and to clarify any questions you have (30 minutes) A technical test for you to complete in your own time (up to 2 hours) followed by a review and technical interview with the Hiring Manager (1 hour) An on-site interview with wider team members focused on system design, ways of working and values alignment We’ll review applications as they’re received and invite suitable candidates to an initial conversation on a rolling basis. If you’re shortlisted, you should be prepared to discuss and expand on your responses during the interview. Bear in mind that hiring teams read a large number of applications. Responses that rely heavily on AI can sometimes feel generic, so taking the time to make your application personal and specific will help it stand out.
